newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Gawler Craton loses place in the sun.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Gawler Craton loses place in the sun.

text.p: South Australia's gold hot spot, the Gawler Craton, appears to have lost its place in the sun among investors, and a new round of exploration reports are not expected to restore the gloss to the region.

However, explorers and analysts say Gawler should not be written off and that only deeper drilling will reveal the depth of the potential under the vast, sandy desert cover which was previously proclaimed as Australia's last gold frontier.

The market has not been kind to Gawler stocks in recent months after an initial frenzy following promising finds at Helix Ltd's Tunkillia deposit last year, and the weather too has been offside, particularly recent heavy rain.
"The rain slowed them all down, so results we were expecting this quarterly just are not going to happen until the next," Macquarie Equities Ltd analyst Paul Barnes told Reuters.
"I do not think the market is terribly patient and (the Gawler stocks) will probably suffer as a result," he said.

With results due over the next ten days, Helix has sought to play down high expectations while news from the Resolute Samantha Ltd -Dominion Mining Ltd joint venture of a mineable resource at the Challenger deposit still looks distant.
"I think you are looking at really another six months drilling before you know if you have a mine or not," Resolute investor relations manager Jim McAuliffe said last week.

An analyst, who did not want to be named, said market interest would wane if Helix did not come up with good results and Challenger did not produce a half a million-plus ounce resource in the short-term, although he said other explorers could still come up with suprising results for the quarter.
"If nobody comes through with any good results, then I think quite clearly there will be consensus in the market that this Gawler thing is a bit of a dead duck," he said.

Major gold producer Acacia Ltd, which paid A$38 million for a 17.4 percent Helix stake in February and has since moved to a 19.9 percent holding - just short of the takeover threshold - believes some market expectations are unrealistic.
Acacia corporate development manager Allan Brash said the company would be looking to Helix's quarterly report for evidence of extensions to the mineralised system at Tunkillia.

"When you have got gold mineralisation determined over 5.7 km already, with surface indications in the order of 12 km and that is only the main anomaly .... the chances of eventually pulling together something very large in it are unusually high
in exploration terms," he said.

Other juniors less advanced in drilling in Gawler but seen by analysts to have good prospects include Equinox Resources Ltd, with ground on the Yarlbrinda shear zone which hosts Helix's find, Grenfell Resources at the old Tarcoola gold field, and Minotaur Gold Ltd which is expected to soon report drilling results from its Birthday prospect.

Analysts and explorers agreed the bearish market and falling gold prices had contributed to negative sentiment on Gawler, compounded by the serious uncertainties around Canadian miner Bre-X Mineral Ltd's Busang gold property in Indonesia.
"Clearly in this environment, in this market, people are a little bit wary of junior explorers," one said.

However, there is agreement that the Gawler Craton, a vast underexplored area of 350,000 square km, remains highly prospective, mainly for gold and copper, but also with potential for uranium, platinum, base metals, nickel and diamonds.

But while aeromagnetic surveys and new calcrete sampling techniques have helped dust away its deep sand cover, geologists are only just beginning to understand the structures of the region and deeper drilling is in its very early stages.
"These guys are working from scratch, they have to start back at square one and work their way through," Jeff Ion from the Perth-based broker Todd Partners said.

"But the explorers are still very fired up, a number raised cash when their shares were up in value, a lot have significant exploration funds and they intend to pour a lot into the ground this year," he said.
-- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
